correctness.rationale: Every indicator has radius-one support. Under one forced extremum, the peak-count law is unchanged by vertex transitivity. Mixed cumulants vanish for disconnected distance-at-most-two dependency graphs; a connected tuple of k supports cannot meet two vertices farther than 2k. The two forced effects therefore cancel against the one-endpoint conditions and yield the stated cumulant and moment equality. The unconditional hypercube variance follows from exact distance-one and distance-two pair probabilities. Independent checker confirms 29 exact finite assertions; no finite check is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Local maximum counts quantify ruggedness of random fitness landscapes, while forcing global extrema at distant genotypes is a natural model for studying adaptive accessibility. The proven distance-controlled invariance protects an expanding hierarchy of fluctuation moments in high dimension despite nontrivial endpoint constraints. The Q2 mean and Q4 variance failures give motivated sharp boundaries at the first two moment orders, demonstrating why the 2r separation matters.
